title: Finite reduction comparisons preserve the strict open-unit transpose
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a Noetherian adic datum with finite perfect quotients $P_n=A/I^n$ and completed coefficient sheaves $A_V=\lim_n(P_n)_V$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow T,j':U'\hookrightarrow T',u:T'\to T,v:U'\to U)$ be a cartesian open square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Work on small pro-etale ringed sites and strict tower derived categories. Use the exact open adjunctions $J_j\dashv j^*$, $J_{j'}\dashv j'^*$ [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], derived strict-tower pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and scalar restriction $r_V$ along $\underline A_V\to A_V$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For any $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$, let $K_\bullet$ be its strict reduction tower and use the canonical open-tensor identification $(j_!K)_\bullet\simeq J_jK_\bullet$. Put
$$Q=Lu^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(j_!K)_\bullet,\quad C=Lv^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet,\quad M=r_UK_\bullet,\quad H=G_vM,\quad N=G_uJ_jM.$$
Here $G,J$ on constant-$A$ towers are [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Fix the canonical finite-reduction/scalar comparisons $a:r_{T'}Q\simeq N$ and $d:r_{U'}C\simeq H$ of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], using the open-tensor unit normalization [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Let $e:r_{T'}J_{j'}C\simeq J_{j'}r_{U'}C$ be the comparison induced by the identity of the underlying extension-by-zero presheaves before abelian sheafification [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and put $b=J_{j'}(d)e$. Let $c:r_{U'}j'^*\simeq G_{j'}r_{T'}$ be the canonical scalar/restriction identification. For $x:C\to j'^*Q$ define
$$\Psi(x)=G_{j'}(a)\circ c_Q\circ r_{U'}(x)\circ d^{-1}:H\to G_{j'}N.$$
The specified comparisons intertwine the two open-adjunction transposes:
$$a\circ r_{T'}(\operatorname{adj}_{A}(x))\circ b^{-1}=\varepsilon'_N\circ J_{j'}(\Psi(x)),$$
where $\operatorname{adj}_{A}(x):J_{j'}C\to Q$ is the completed-ring transpose and $\varepsilon'$ is the constant-$A$ open counit [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. If $x$ is the pullback by $v$ of the open unit of $K_\bullet$, followed by the inverse-image square compositor and the specified quotient/open source identification, then
$$\Psi(x)=G_v(\eta_M)\text{ followed by }G_vG_jJ_jM\simeq G_{j'}G_uJ_jM,$$
where $\eta_M:M\to G_jJ_jM$ is the constant-$A$ open unit. Both identities are induced on simultaneous strict diagram representatives, commute with all quotient transitions, and descend to their unbounded derived categories. They are natural in $K$ and in $x$. No completeness, quasi-compactness, origin witness or bound on cohomological degrees is required.

proof.text: Naturality of exchangeResPull transports unitArrow through the source, corner and quotient/open comparisons, cancelling their inverses. Apply restrictionSquare to move the integral square through scalar restriction. Naturality of the v scalar comparison moves the open unit to the constant side. Naturality of constantSquare moves the scalar/open comparison across the square. Apply the unit equation of scalarMate under the constant v pullback and compose with the square component. This direct calculation proves the second conjunct on whole derived strict towers, retaining all transitions and using no faithfulness of evaluation, flatness, completeness, or boundedness. The private scalarSquareUnit lemma treats the compositor as a parameter during this calculation and is then applied to the specified constantSquare; this prevents expansion of the derived compositors without changing their value. Transport both endpoints along the equality between scalar restriction of the reduction object and restricted.obj K before composing these identities. Reflexive endpoint transports cancel. This keeps the fixed derived compositor folded throughout the object conversion.
